messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: auth-anomaly-detector triggered on auth-proxy (high vol from 35.189.24.0/22). 5000 requests/min to /v1/session_create. Severity: high. Link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/2987654322

alice.b: saw this alert, routing to on-call. Tagging sec/ops.

dave_oncall: I'm on it. Correlating with recent deploy? Checking ingress ACLs and WAF.

sasha_sec: thanks @dave_oncall. Can you confirm whether tokens were returned in logs? We saw a small spike in w/embedding-service earlier.

dave_oncall: quick grep on recent log archive says a handful (~12) of auth debug logs contain session_id fields and partial headers. Not full tokens but headers printed. Could be staging vs prod config drift.

miguel_sre: blocking offending /v1/session_create path from that CIDR at the LB layer now: `curl -X POST https://ops.redwood/run -d '{"action":"block_cidr","cidr":"35.189.24.0/22"}'` -> started. 

sasha_sec: good. Also start emergency key rotation for service account used by embedding-service (svc-embed-runner). Potential exposure vector.

dave_oncall: initiating rotation. Steps: 1) revoke current key on KMS console, 2) create new key, 3) update deployment secret on dedicated and hosted secrets stores, 4) perform rolling restart. Running command: ```./scripts/rotate_svc_key.sh svc-embed-runner --env prod --force```

aleah_legal: flagging for incident record — if logs had headers with user IDs we need to assess customer impact before any external notice. Please capture which customers had session creation attempts.

jamie_cust: customer success here — let me know if we need to open P1 bridge with any affected enterprise customers.

dave_oncall: quick customer-impact query: `SELECT customer_id, count(*) FROM auth_logs WHERE path='/v1/session_create' AND ts > now()-interval '1 hour' GROUP BY customer_id;` returning three internal test accounts and one real customer (cust_acme) with 7 hits.
sasha_sec: cust_acme alerted. We should treat those 7 as potential exposure to header values. Start targeted log scrub and redact in storage. Also trigger encrypted log reingest to avoid accidental exfil.
miguel_sre: rotation script ran, new secret pushed to 2 out of 3 clusters successfully. Canary restart on cluster-a healthy. cluster-b still pulling old secret — investigating.
dave_oncall: cluster-b had stale secret controller, manual patch applied. Rolling restart done. All services now using new key.
sasha_sec: confirm old key revoked in KMS?
dave_oncall: confirmed, old key schedule set to disabled immediately. KMS audit id: kms-audit-2987.
aleah_legal: please capture timeline for postmortem. We may need to notify regulators if PII leaked. Documented who had access to logs and retention windows.
jamie_cust: reaching out to cust_acme account rep to prep a message in case they escalate. No external message yet.
dave_oncall: mitigation checklist: LB block in place, key rotated, logs redacted and archived, canary restarts healthy, WAF rules tightened to block this UA pattern.
sasha_sec: assigning follow-ups: miguel_sre to complete log scrub (ETA 2h), dave_oncall to own canary verification (ETA 30m), leah_legal to draft internal notification (ETA 1h), jamie_cust to keep cust_acme on standby.
miguel_sre: scrub started. Using redaction pipeline: `redact-logs --pattern 'Authorization: .*' --run --from 2987654000 --to 2987654322`

dave_oncall: verification OK on canary, latency and error rates normal. No elevated 5xx post-rotation.
sasha_sec: running deeper forensics now — pulling flow logs and origin ASNs. If we see lateral movement, escalate to full incident response.
aleah_legal: thanks. Keep me posted. Also capture any PagerDuty escalation notes for legal record.
jamie_cust: update — cust_acme rep says they saw odd session resets earlier; prepping a joint call if we confirm data exposure.
dave_oncall: last update: LB block remains, KMS rotation complete, logs scrubbed + archived, WAF rule applied. Creating incident ticket IR-2026-2987. Will start post-incident RCA thread after forensics.

incident-bot: Incident ticket created IR-2026-2987. On-call handover will occur in 50m to next rotation. React with :thumbsup: when handed off.
